Packet anatomy

Settlement readiness depends on proof, billing support, driver review, and cash-flow context.

Each packet item below is demo content. It shows what the record is, who usually provides it, why the fleet needs it, and what happens when it is missing before settlement or billing release.

Packet itemWhat it isWho provides itWhy it mattersIf missing
Proof PacketPOD, BOL, dock photos, seal/cargo proof, receiver notes, and closeout evidence.Driver, dispatcher, customer, receiver, or packet owner.Confirms the work was completed and supports invoice/settlement review.Settlement and invoice readiness move to hold or review.
Billing PacketInvoice support, rate confirmation, POD, accessorial approval, and customer billing notes.Customer, dispatcher, billing owner, and document reviewer.Shows why the invoice is ready and which records support charges.Billing cannot confidently release; receivables follow-up may wait.
Driver Settlement VerificationPay basis, miles, stop pay, bonus, reimbursement, deduction, and reviewer note.Operations, payroll coordinator, contractor settlement owner, or finance reviewer.Connects pay lines to trip records without pretending BOF is payroll.Pay stays in review until the fleet's proper reviewer confirms support.
POD / Lumper / Rate ConfirmationSigned delivery proof, lumper receipt, and agreed commercial terms.Driver, receiver, lumper provider, broker/customer, or packet owner.Supports payment, reimbursement, and rate-backed billing.Invoice, reimbursement, or factoring packet may remain incomplete.
Detention / AccessorialsApproved waiting time, extra stop, layover, toll, or other supported charge.Dispatcher, customer, driver, or billing owner.Shows why an extra charge or pay line belongs in the packet.Accessorial pay or invoice lines remain under review.
Deductions / Fuel AdvancesAdvance, equipment, damage, fuel, or other deduction support.Finance, fleet owner, settlement owner, or contractor record owner.Keeps deduction logic reviewable before money is released.Settlement statement should not finalize without support.
Claims HoldsClaim flag, damage note, photo evidence, incident record, and owner review.Safety, claims owner, driver, customer, or receiver.Prevents payout or billing from ignoring unresolved risk.Settlement, invoice, or factoring readiness may stay on hold.
Factoring Packet SupportInvoice, rate confirmation, POD, packet completeness, and exception state.Billing owner, finance reviewer, or factoring coordination owner.Shows whether receivable support is ready for the fleet's factoring process.Cash-flow visibility remains uncertain until packet gaps clear.

Load-to-Settlement Trace

A settlement packet starts with the load record, not a loose pay formula.

BOF keeps the settlement trail connected to the assigned load, driver, invoice, POD status, receipt support, and factoring packet readiness. The packet can show why money is ready, under review, or held without pretending to run payroll or factoring.

Load assigned Driver completes work POD and receipts collected Invoice prepared Factoring packet checked Settlement packet calculated Payroll or contractor review

Settlement command center

Every settlement status explains the pay rule, packet condition, and operating blocker.

BOF does not simply collect PODs. BOF connects trucking settlement documents, driver pay calculations, cents-per-mile pay, contractor settlement statements, POD billing delays, factoring packet readiness, post-trip paperwork, driver settlement holds, payroll coordination, receivables, and cash-flow visibility into one reviewable operating record.

Pay Type Engine

BOF can show the pay basis, formula, support documents, and exception state before release.

The settlement view supports multiple driver and contractor pay structures without turning the static demo into live payroll processing. Each formula is demo data that shows how records, review, reimbursements, deductions, and packet readiness can be organized for the fleet team.

Cents-per-mile pay2,140 miles × $0.62 = $1,326.80

Uses loaded miles, rate, trip record, and payroll review status.

Percentage pay25% of $4,850 linehaul = $1,212.50

Shows percentage of linehaul or invoice without implying final payroll advice.

Stop pay3 extra stops × $50 = $150.00

Requires stop count and supporting trip notes.

Backhaul payBackhaul incentive = $325.00

Connects backhaul incentive to dispatch and settlement review.

Safety bonusSafety bonus eligible = $175.00

Depends on safety status and reviewable record notes.

Detention / layover4 hours × $35 = $140.00

Needs detention approval and customer billing support.

ReimbursementsLumper reimbursement = $240.00

Requires receipt, packet match, and reimbursement review.

DeductionsAdvance deduction = -$150.00

Keeps deduction note and approval trail visible.

Employee payroll coordinationPayroll review linked to wage, bonus, and reimbursement support

BOF organizes records for review; payroll decisions stay with the proper provider and fleet process.

Independent contractor settlement statementSettlement statement linked to W-9, invoice support, and deductions

Contractor settlement records stay inspectable before release.

Settlement holdMissing POD = payout held for review

Missing delivery proof keeps the settlement from appearing release-ready.

Factoring impactIncomplete packet = receivable not ready for factoring review

Packet readiness connects settlement documents to receivables visibility.

Employee and contractor workflows

One settlement screen can separate employee payroll coordination from independent contractor settlement review.

BOF keeps the record logic visible while respecting the boundary between workflow support and professional payroll, tax, legal, accounting, banking, factoring, or classification decisions.

Employee

Employee Payroll Coordination

  • Payroll review
  • Wage, bonus, and reimbursement support
  • HR record connection
  • Training and safety status
  • Payroll exception review
  • Benefits and payroll coordination visibility, where applicable
Contractor

Independent Contractor Settlement

  • Settlement statement
  • W-9 / contractor document status
  • Invoice or settlement packet
  • Deductions and reimbursements
  • 1099-style support records
  • Contractor settlement review

Boundary: BOF supports settlement workflow coordination, records, visibility, packet readiness, and review. BOF does not replace payroll, tax, legal, accounting, banking, factoring, or employment-classification professionals.

Settlement holds and exceptions

Held money should show the reason, owner, and downstream cash-flow impact.

A driver settlement hold is not useful if it only says "hold." BOF shows whether the issue is document readiness, safety review, payroll exception, contractor paperwork, claim evidence, detention approval, or a deduction note.

Missing POD Settlement hold Factoring packet incomplete Receivable not ready Cash-flow impact

Factoring and cash-flow visibility

Settlement documents also explain invoice readiness and receivables follow-through.

When a post-trip packet is incomplete, the issue can affect payroll coordination, contractor settlement statements, invoice readiness, factoring packet readiness, receivables visibility, payment timing, and billing follow-through. BOF keeps those connections visible.

Post-trip packet complete Invoice ready Factoring packet ready Receivable visibility Cash-flow follow-through

Packet readiness

Rate confirmation, signed POD, lumper or detention proof, claim clearance, invoice support, and settlement notes appear as one packet condition.

Receivables view

Fleet leaders can see whether billing, factoring coordination, or cash-flow follow-through is waiting on the same record that holds settlement review.

Careful role language

BOF supports factoring coordination, packet readiness, receivables visibility, and cash-flow follow-through. BOF is not the factoring company, lender, bank, or accounting firm.
